dedupe_keys.name: isi wfp food insecurity forecasting model gradient boosted forecasts of insufficient food consumption up to 30 days ahead burkina faso cameroon mali nigeria syria yemen

description: This model forecasts, up to a month ahead, what share of people in each province of six fragile countries will not eat enough, so that food assistance can be positioned before a crisis deepens. It was built by Pietro Foini, Michele Tizzoni, Giulia Martini, Daniela Paolotti and Elisa Omodei at the ISI Foundation with the World Food Programme and published in Scientific Reports in 2023. Coverage is Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Mali, three north-eastern states of Nigeria, Syria and Yemen, using the daily remote-monitoring series behind WFP's HungerMap. Gradient boosted regression trees take past food consumption and coping indicators with conflict fatalities, cereal prices, rainfall, vegetation anomalies and the Ramadan calendar, and the repository also holds correlation and permutation-entropy analyses of how forecastable each series is. The Python code and data pipelines are available as a free download from GitHub under the MIT licence, with a conda environment file. Caveats: forecasts rest on phone-survey data with possible sampling bias, horizons are short, and the repository has not been updated since publication. Simulation uses: an early-warning layer that feeds food supply disruption and humanitarian response models with expected changes in need. Related records: the Harmonized Food Insecurity Dataset (data-harmonized-food-insecurity-dataset) supplies comparable sub-national indicators.
